feeds.dataset: OSDR Rodent Research-1 ISS environmental telemetry, 2014
feeds.time_basis: Dataset clock as printed in the source file. The source states no time zone, so the printed time is carried with a Z suffix as the dataset's own clock and is not asserted to be UTC.

source.text: The file carries no cabin pressure. NASA-SOURCES.md section 2 states the 760 mmHg assumption used to convert ppm to mmHg.

file.text: Byte copy of eda_rr1_telemetry.csv (SHA-256 in provenance.json). Column co2_iss is the ISS channel CO2 in ppm.

unit.text: units_from_portal_js in eda_rr1_provenance.json: co2_iss is ppm. Wire spelling ppm; UCUM [ppm] by config/unit-mapping.json.

time_basis.text: timestamp_timezone in eda_rr1_provenance.json: not stated in the downloaded payload; not assumed UTC.

window.text: Seven days of the file ending 2014-10-07 15:36, the demo replay clock (DEMO-CONDITIONS.md); 2012 rows, the original dates kept.

pace.text: Burst: the demo does not wait five minutes per sample. Freshness follows hub receive time of rows that advance the window end (D14).

feeds.time_basis: Dataset clock as printed in the source file. The API states no time zone, so the printed time is carried with a Z suffix as the dataset's own clock and is not asserted to be UTC.

file.text: Byte copy of radlab_dostel_sample.csv (SHA-256 in provenance.json). Only DosTel1 rows: an instrument dose rate in the Columbus module, never a person's dose.

unit.text: absorbed_dose_rate_units in radlab_dostel_sample.provenance.json: microgray per hour.

time_basis.text: timestamp_timezone in radlab_dostel_sample.provenance.json: not stated by the API; not asserted.

pace.text: Burst, as for the RR-1 feed.

source.text: The twin streams ppm. NASA-SOURCES.md section 2 states the 760 mmHg assumption used to convert ppm to mmHg.

sim.text: The habitat simulator twin replays the RR-1 ISS CO2 recording as Bluetooth Environmental Sensing notifications; the adapter parses the same bytes a real sensor would send. The device identity declares it simulated.

pace.text: One notification every 5 s, the catalog CO2 interval (EV01).
